title: We’re Not in World War III Yet, Realist John Mearsheimer Explains | Endgame #258
summary: A realist scholar argues WW3 has not begun, blames NATO's 2008 Ukraine pledge for the war, and says the Iran and Ukraine wars drain the US effort against China and spur proliferation.

assertions.quote: No. I think to be in World War II, China and the United States would have to be at war
the United States has been waging a proxy war against Russia in Ukraine that is much more uh much more forceful uh much more intense

verdicts.note: Western arms and intelligence support for Ukraine has few Cold War parallels, but Soviet roles in Korea and Vietnam make 'more intense than any' a stretch, and 'proxy war' is a contested label.

assertions.quote: If we had not decided to do this, Ukraine, I believe, would be intact today inside inside its original borders.
you can see how that war against Iran and the war in Ukraine is in a very important way damaging our ability to contain China

verdicts.note: Munitions and interceptors spent in Ukraine and the Middle East come from the same limited stocks needed in the Pacific, though most US naval and air power in Asia stays in place.

assertions.quote: But the Ukraine war has pushed the Russians and the Chinese together.

verdicts.note: Since 2022 China has become Russia's main trade partner and supplier of dual-use goods and the two declared a 'no limits' partnership, though China has sent no weapons or troops.

DoD 2025: China and Russia deepened their partnership and defense engagement in 2024, with Beijing a 'critical enabler' of Russia's war through diplomatic, defense-industrial and economic support amid sanctions.
DDIS: Russia's dependence on China has deepened since the war, with about half its imports now from China against a quarter before, and military cooperation expected to continue after the war.
US intelligence says sanctions resilience comes at the cost of Russia's deepening dependence on China, a closer but unequal alignment.

assertions.quote: China and Russia are with Iran, not in any meaningful way at this point
in private all sorts of people in South Korea and in Japan are talking about getting nuclear weapons
if you look at the scholarly literature on decapitation, right? And there's an extensive literature on this. It makes it clear that it never works

verdicts.note: Studies of leadership decapitation find it seldom produces surrender or regime collapse on its own, but 'never works' overstates a mixed literature.
In the 2026 Iran war, eliminating the leadership produced a more hardline leadership and continued refusal to submit; one case consistent with the claim, not a base rate.

assertions.quote: at some point you'll get an armistice like you did in Korea in 1953. You'll get some sort of frozen conflict

verdicts.note: Most forecasters expect any end to the fighting to be a ceasefire along the front line without a settled peace, but the war has not ended so the prediction is unresolved.
52% of the surveyed strategists expect the Ukraine war to become a frozen conflict (up from 43%), against 34% expecting terms favourable to Russia.
